ClassificationResult.description:
Full duplicate-adjudication output for a report pair.

The decision logic answers two sequential questions:

* ``independence_assessment`` — did the two reports arise
  independently? Independence is rejected either on direct evidence
  of shared provenance (a shared source identifier) or when the
  rarity-based matching evidence is strong enough to reject the
  null hypothesis that the reports are independent draws from the
  comparison population.
* ``relationship_assessment`` — for non-independent pairs, do the
  reports describe the same underlying case (``Same_case``), a
  demonstrably different case (``Different_case``), or is the
  evidence insufficient to safely resolve the question
  (``Abstain``)?

Use ``final_label`` for the user-facing label (``Duplicates`` /
``Otherwise_related`` / ``Unrelated`` / ``Abstain``); downstream
consumers should depend on this rather than on the raw internal
fields. ``penalty`` is the exception: it is diagnostic, carried so that
the inconsistency arithmetic behind the decision can be displayed and
audited without reconstructing it.
ClassificationResult.title: ClassificationResult

InconsistencyPenalty.description:
The weighted inconsistency score, and the comparison the decision made.

    w_tot = Σ (count × weight)  over the severities present

Self-describing by design: the classifier is the only component that knows
both the inconsistency counts and the configured weights, so it records the
result rather than leaving consumers to recompute it. Recomputing requires
the run's ``DecisionThresholds``, and a consumer that assumes the defaults
will silently disagree with the decision whenever the run used custom
weights.

``threshold`` is the bar this score was tested against, or ``None`` when the
decision made no ``w_tot`` comparison at all — the below-limited zone (where
``L_match`` decides) and ``SAME_SOURCE_DIFFERENT_CASE`` (pinned regardless of
``w_tot``). In those cases the score is still recorded; there is simply no
comparison to report.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Relationship assessment
InconsistencyPenalty.title: InconsistencyPenalty

InconsistencySeverity.description:
Severity levels for detected inconsistencies between reports.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Severity levels

Levels:
    minor     – small difference, weakly suggests different individuals
    moderate  – meaningful difference, weakens the duplicate hypothesis
    strong    – strongly suggests different individuals
    decisive  – forces Different classification (e.g. distinct
                patient IDs from the same study in the narratives)
InconsistencySeverity.title: InconsistencySeverity

IndependenceAssessment.description:
Internal independence assessment produced by the decision logic.

Captures whether the pair's independence can be rejected: either
directly, via a reliable shared source identifier (shared
provenance), or via the rarity-based matching evidence — a
``NON_INDEPENDENT`` verdict then means the matched features are too
unlikely to have arisen by chance if the reports were independent
draws from the comparison population. The same-case vs
different-case distinction is made separately by the
``RelationshipAssessment``.

The user-facing label is derived from this enum (plus
``RelationshipAssessment``) by ``ClassificationResult.final_label``;
downstream consumers should depend on the final label rather than
on this raw enum.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Independence assessment
IndependenceAssessment.title: IndependenceAssessment

IndependenceReason.description:
Audit trail for which branch in the decision logic fired.

Attached to :class:`ClassificationResult` so downstream review can
tell *why* a pair landed on its independence assessment. The
``RARITY_*`` values correspond to the four L_match zones of the
rarity-based matching evidence; ``SHARED_SOURCE`` means independence
was rejected on direct evidence of shared provenance (a reliable
shared source identifier derived from the narratives, or a
shared-source verdict from the source-case comparison).

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Independence assessment
IndependenceReason.title: IndependenceReason

PairPrediction.description:
The frozen prediction for one pair.

``adjudicator_label`` is the evaluated method's decided outcome.
``screening_retrieved`` is whether the upstream screening method flagged the
pair as a candidate; ``None`` means no screening result was supplied. The
field is read only for sets with ``screening_mode: observed``, where
:mod:`llm_dup_dev.study_eval.preflight` requires it — a
``not_evaluated`` set neither needs it nor reads it, so the same prediction
record can serve a pair belonging to sets of both modes.
``classification`` is the optional full decision trace (the same
``ClassificationResult`` the pipeline produces); when present it is checked
for consistency with ``adjudicator_label`` and ``pair_id``.
PairPrediction.title: PairPrediction

PenaltyTerm.description:
One severity's contribution to ``w_tot``.

Carries the ``weight`` **actually applied** by the run, not the default,
so the arithmetic can be reproduced from the result alone.
PenaltyTerm.title: PenaltyTerm

RelationshipAssessment.description:
Relationship assessment for pairs whose independence was rejected.

Answers the second adjudication question: do the two reports
describe the same underlying case (``SAME_CASE``), or is the pair
linked by something other than being the same individual case —
e.g. same reporter, same study, two patients on the same unusual
regimen (``DIFFERENT_CASE``)? The decision logic chooses based on
the inconsistency signals (weighted score ``w_tot``) interpreted
against the strength of the matching evidence and the source
context.

``ABSTAIN`` is emitted for epistemically underdetermined
same-source scenarios: non-independence is established (same source
identifier confirmed) but the available evidence is insufficient to
safely determine whether the reports describe the same individual.

``ClassificationResult.final_label`` maps these to the user-facing
labels: ``Same_case`` → ``Duplicates``, ``Different_case`` →
``Otherwise_related``, ``Abstain`` → ``Abstain``.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Relationship assessment
RelationshipAssessment.title: RelationshipAssessment

description:
A frozen bundle of per-pair predictions from one method configuration.

One bundle corresponds to one frozen run/configuration. The abstain- and
otherwise-related-positive *re-interpretation* secondary analyses do not need
a new bundle — they re-read this one under a different positivity rule (see
:mod:`llm_dup_dev.study_eval.aggregate`). A configuration that produces
genuinely different classifications (e.g. an LLM-based component swap) arrives
as a second bundle with a distinct ``configuration_id``.

``predictions`` is keyed by ``pair_id``.
title: PredictionSet
